tess: Heads up — noticed a cluster of 401s from our background workers after the nightly k8s secret swap. workers are long-lived async tasks using a shared AsyncClient.

natalie: can you drop the smallest repro and logs?

tess: yep. simplified pattern: one AsyncClient() instance, many coroutines call client.chat() in a loop. When we update the REDWOOD_API_KEY via a secret rollout the pod env var changes but the process keeps using the old key until restart. we see a spike of 401s for ~20-40s.

tess: log paste:
```
2026-03-21T00:04:12Z INFO run_id=xyz1 POST /v1/chat 200 85ms
2026-03-21T00:04:16Z INFO run_id=xyz2 POST /v1/chat 200 90ms
2026-03-21T00:04:19Z WARN run_id=xyz3 POST /v1/chat 401 12ms error=invalid_api_key
2026-03-21T00:04:20Z WARN run_id=xyz4 POST /v1/chat 401 14ms error=invalid_api_key
2026-03-21T00:04:35Z INFO run_id=xyz9 POST /v1/chat 200 92ms
```

sahil: sounds like authorization headers are stuck on pooled connections/HTTP2 streams. which http client is AsyncClient wrapping?

tess: we use httpx AsyncClient underneath with http2 enabled. client is created like:
```py
client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
# long-running process, tasks call client.chat(...) repeatedly
```

natalie: two separate issues: (1) UX for rotating creds without restarting processes, (2) types + convenience for pluggable auth sources.

sahil: agreed. proposal: accept an auth factory/callable instead of only a static api_key. something like `auth_provider` that can be sync or async and returns headers. default remains `api_key` for simple users.

tess: +1. also want per-call override so a single client can be used for transient API keys: `client.chat(..., api_key=...)`. creating many clients is heavy because of connection pools.

natalie: implementation notes: resolve headers immediately before sending each request so the active header is fresh. but avoid allocating expensive objects per-request — accept a callable and only call it once per HTTP request. support both sync and async callables in typing.

sahil: also add `on_401` hook: when we get a 401, the client should ask the provider for fresh headers and retry once for idempotent endpoints. make this opt-in via `refresh_on_401=True` to be safe for non-idempotent ops.

tess: do we need to drain / recreate connections to avoid reusing HTTP/2 streams that still have old header state?

sahil: good point. when a retry after refresh happens we should open a new connection for the retry instead of reusing the same transport that returned 401. httpx has options to close and re-establish pools; expose a safe helper like `_new_connection_for_retry()`. document the semantics clearly.

natalie: typing: add a Protocol `AuthProvider` with `def __call__(self) -> Mapping[str, str]` or `async def __call__(self) -> Mapping[str,str]`. stubs should show `auth_provider: Optional[AuthProvider] = None`. Also ensure `AsyncClient` implements `AsyncContextManager[AsyncClient]` in type stubs.

tess: telemetry idea: emit a metric when we see a burst of 401s attributed to key change (e.g., `sdk.auth.consecutive_401s`), maybe tag with pod and route. ops can alert on it.

sahil: I'll prototype API shape: `AsyncClient(*, api_key: Optional[str]=None, auth_provider: Optional[AuthProvider]=None, refresh_on_401: bool=False)` and per-request `client.chat(..., api_key=..., auth_provider=...)`. tests: simulate provider swapping mid-flight.

natalie: docs: add a cookbook entry "Handling key rotation in long-running processes" with examples: EnvProvider, KMS-backed provider, and per-request override. include guidance on idempotency and retry.

ops-bot: CI started for branch sahil/async-auth-fix (job 4789) :gear:

tess: thanks — i'll attach a tiny docker-compose + script that triggers secret change and reproduces the pooling behaviour. will include a short test that confirms pools reuse.

sahil: great, tagging @devex and @eng-runtime. i'll open a draft PR with types + small integration test. feedback welcome.

tess: also can we add a debug flag to the client to log auth header resolution for a short window? would make it quicker to triage in prod.

natalie: ok but default off for PII. debug-only, scrub tokens in logs.

tess: agreed. thanks all, will upload repro in ~20m. :+1:
